f_a^{\mathrm{ID}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y).
\tag{2}
\]
Hence the coordinate is constant on the observed-law fiber. By \(\text{lem:semialgebraic-fiber-dichotomy}\), the unique TCF cell is identifying. The storage rule in \(\text{def:tcf-procedure}\) verifies the candidate against \(\mathsf V_{a,y}\), so (2) implies that the cell carries exactly \(f_a^{\mathrm{ID}}\). The argument establishes the stated one-way reduction only; the pointwise CAD may still refine the ordinary graphwise dichotomy.

statements.statement: Whenever \(\operatorname{RC}(\mathcal G,A,Y)\) holds and every context-specific graph is identifying, delayed restriction is unnecessary. For every compatible \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), its unique TCF partition cell is identifying and, for every \(a,y\), carries exactly \(f_a^{\mathrm{RC}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\). No converse is asserted for identification at one exceptional observed law.
statements.justification: The reduction locates the new difficulty precisely in endogenous missingness and observed-proxy traces.
statements.gap: Mokhtarian et al. prove completeness for observed root controls; their proof does not cover endogenous indicators, proxy censoring, or fix-before-select traces.
statements.consumer: Users can retain the simpler context-by-context algorithm whenever its published root-control conditions hold.
statements.proof_tex:
Assume \(\operatorname{RC}(\mathcal G,A,Y)\). Let \(C_{\mathrm{ctx}}\) denote the finite vector of observed root context variables. Because it has no parents, intervention on \(A\) does not change its distribution. The context-recovery result \(\text{lem:root-control-context-recovery}\) gives, for every compatible model,
\[
\begin{aligned}
Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)
&=\sum_cP_{\mathrm{obs}}(C_{\mathrm{ctx}}=c)
f_{a,c}^{\mathrm{ID}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\\
&=f_a^{\mathrm{RC}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y).
\end{aligned}
\tag{1}
\]
The assumed identification of every context graph supplies every \(f_{a,c}^{\mathrm{ID}}\), and positivity supplies the context conditionals on their support.

Since context variables are observed roots, restricting to \(C_{\mathrm{ctx}}=c\) does not discard a parent mechanism needed to form an earlier intervention kernel. The TCF recursion may therefore take the context restriction first, reproduce each ordinary-ID operation word in that context, and average the resulting kernels with the observed root probabilities. This branch supplies the rational candidate on the second line of (1), so delayed restriction is unnecessary in this submodel.

Equation (1) holds for every \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\); therefore the coordinate is constant on that fiber. By \(\text{lem:semialgebraic-fiber-dichotomy}\), the unique TCF cell is identifying. The verified-storage rule of \(\text{def:tcf-procedure}\), together with (1), shows that its value is exactly \(f_a^{\mathrm{RC}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\) for every \((a,y)\). This proves the reduction and makes no converse claim about exceptional observed laws.

statements.statement: The universal binary-witness assertion is false, and the smallest substantive alphabet vector is not determined by the color and district structure of a colored hedge alone. There exist a finite regular-maximal graph \(\mathcal G\), a hedge in \(\operatorname{CH}(\mathcal G,A,Y)\), and a strictly positive compatible \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) for which two models in \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) have different \(Q_a\), but no model matching \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) can make every substantive variable binary. More generally, an always-observed substantive coordinate requires at least the cardinality of its observed support, and a partially observed coordinate \(Z\) requires at least \(|\operatorname{supp}(Z^{\dagger}\mid R_Z=1)|\). Under strict positivity these lower bounds equal the declared substantive alphabet cardinalities.
statements.proof_tex:
We give a direct finite counterexample and then prove the support assertions.

Let \(\mathcal V=\{A,Y,Z\}\), let \(\mathcal R=\varnothing\), let \(\mathcal X_A=\mathcal X_Y=\{0,1\}\), and let \(\mathcal X_Z=\{0,1,2\}\).  Thus every substantive variable is always observed and \(\mathcal O=(A,Y,Z)\).  Let \(\mathcal G\) have the directed edge \(A\to Y\), the bidirected edge \(A\leftrightarrow Y\), isolated vertex \(Z\), and empty label set.  Its directed part is acyclic, as required by ass:acyclic.  Because \(\mathcal R=\varnothing\), there is no missingness context in which a label could occur; consequently the empty label set is regular and maximal, so ass:regular and ass:maximal hold.  Assumptions ass:proxy-consistency and ass:label-semantics are vacuous for this graph.

Let \(\mathcal F\) be the \(C\)-forest induced by \(\{A,Y\}\), and let \(\mathcal F'\) be its subforest induced by \(\{Y\}\).  The two forests have the same root set \(\{Y\}\), \(\mathcal F\cap\{A\}=\{A\}\), and \(\mathcal F'\cap\{A\}=\varnothing\).  The common root \(Y\) is an ancestor of \(Y\) after intervention on \(A\), since every vertex is its own ancestor.  Take the empty color assignment and the trace family consisting only of the empty trace.  That trace family is prefix closed, and the licensing condition is vacuous because no color occurs.  Hence, by def:colored-hedge,
\[
 H=(\mathcal F,\mathcal F',\varnothing,\{\varnothing\})
 \in \operatorname{CH}(\mathcal G,A,Y).
\]

We next construct two models.  Let \(U\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) be the exogenous factor shared by \(A\) and \(Y\).  Independently, let \(E_A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/4)\), let \(E_Y\) be uniform on \(\{1,\ldots,16\}\), and let \(E_Z\) be uniform on \(\{0,1,2\}\).  Put
\[
 A=U\oplus E_A,
 \qquad
 Z=E_Z,
 \qquad
 t_0=\frac14,
 \qquad
 t_1=-\frac14.
\]
Here \(\oplus\) denotes addition modulo two, and the Bernoulli parameter is the probability of value one.
For \(i\in\{0,1\}\), define
\[
 k_i(u,a)
 =16\left[\frac12+t_i\left\{\mathbf 1(u=a)-\frac34\right\}\right]
\]
and in model \(\mathcal M_i\) set
\[
 Y=\mathbf 1\{E_Y\leq k_i(U,A)\}.
\]
The four possible thresholds are integers: \(k_0(u,a)\) is \(9\) when \(u=a\) and \(5\) otherwise, whereas \(k_1(u,a)\) is \(7\) when \(u=a\) and \(11\) otherwise.  Thus these are deterministic finite response tables.  The equation for \(A\) depends on the shared factor \(U\), and the equation for \(Y\) depends on both \(A\) and \(U\): for either model, changing whether \(u=a\) changes the threshold.  Hence the directed edge and the individual bidirected-edge factor are both active, and no edge other than those of \(\mathcal G\) is introduced.  The exogenous factors are mutually independent, so the construction satisfies ass:semimarkovian; it is compatible with the empty label set and therefore belongs to the published labeled-missingness class.

For positivity, define
\[
 \pi_i(u,a)=\frac{k_i(u,a)}{16}.
\]
The displayed threshold values give \(0<\pi_i(u,a)<1\) for every \(i,u,a\).  Moreover \(P(E_A=e)>0\) for both \(e\in\{0,1\}\).  Therefore, for every \((a,y,z)\in\mathcal X_A\times\mathcal X_Y\times\mathcal X_Z\), independence of the exogenous factors gives
\[
 P_{\mathcal M_i}(A=a,Y=y,Z=z)
 =\frac13\sum_{u=0}^1
 \frac12 P(E_A=a\oplus u)
 \pi_i(u,a)^y\{1-\pi_i(u,a)\}^{1-y}>0.
\]
This verifies ass:strict-positivity cell by cell.  All alphabets are finite, as required by ass:finite-alphabets.  It follows from def:positive-rm-class that
\[
 \mathcal M_0,\mathcal M_1\in
 \mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G).
\]

We now compute the observed laws.  For either \(a\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 P_{\mathcal M_i}(A=a)
 =\sum_{u=0}^1\frac12P(E_A=a\oplus u)
 =\frac12\left(\frac34+\frac14\right)
 =\frac12,
\]
and
\[
 P_{\mathcal M_i}(U=a,A=a)
 =P(U=a,E_A=0)
 =\frac12\cdot\frac34
 =\frac38.
\]
Division is legitimate because \(P(A=a)=1/2>0\), and hence
\[
 P_{\mathcal M_i}(U=a\mid A=a)=\frac{3/8}{1/2}=\frac34.
\]
Using the response equation for \(Y\) and the law of total probability conditional on \(A=a\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_{\mathcal M_i}(Y=1\mid A=a)
 &=\sum_{u=0}^1
 \left[\frac12+t_i\left\{\mathbf 1(u=a)-\frac34\right\}\right]
 P(U=u\mid A=a)\\
 &=\frac12+t_i\left\{P(U=a\mid A=a)-\frac34\right\}
 =\frac12.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Since \(Z=E_Z\) is independent and uniform, both models consequently induce
\[
 P_{\mathcal M_i}(A=a,Y=y,Z=z)
 =\frac12\cdot\frac12\cdot\frac13
 =\frac1{12}
\]
for every observed cell.  Let \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) denote this common uniform law.

Under \(\operatorname{do}(A=a)\), the equation for \(A\) is replaced by the constant \(a\), while the distribution of \(U\) remains Bernoulli \(\left(1/2\right)\) by the SCM intervention semantics in def:causal-query.  Therefore
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 Q_a^{\mathcal M_i}(1)
 &=\sum_{u=0}^1
 \left[\frac12+t_i\left\{\mathbf 1(u=a)-\frac34\right\}\right]P(U=u)\\
 &=\frac12+t_i\left(\frac12-\frac34\right)
 =\frac12-\frac{t_i}{4}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Thus
\[
 Q_a^{\mathcal M_0}(1)=\frac7{16}
 \qquad\text{and}\qquad
 Q_a^{\mathcal M_1}(1)=\frac9{16}.
\]
By def:observational-fiber, both models lie in \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), but their interventional laws differ.  This proves nonidentification for the displayed colored hedge with strictly positive witnesses.

It remains to prove that no universal binary witness can match this observed law and to establish the general support claim.  If \(W\) is always observed, define
\[
 S_W=\{w:P_{\mathrm{obs}}(W=w)>0\}.
\]
In any model inducing \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), the observed value of \(W\) is its substantive value, so \(S_W\subseteq\mathcal X_W\).  Consequently
\[
 |\mathcal X_W|\geq |S_W|.
\]
For a partially observed substantive coordinate \(W\), ass:proxy-consistency implies on \(R_W=1\) that \(W^{\dagger}=W\).  Hence, whenever \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}(R_W=1)>0\),
\[
 S_W^{\dagger}
 =\operatorname{supp}_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}}(W^{\dagger}\mid R_W=1)
 \subseteq\mathcal X_W,
\]
and therefore
\[
 |\mathcal X_W|\geq |S_W^{\dagger}|.
\]
The required conditioning event has positive probability under ass:strict-positivity: summing the positive full-data cells with \(R_W=1\) gives \(P_{\mathcal M}(R_W=1)>0\).

Under ass:strict-positivity, both inclusions are equalities at the level of supports.  Indeed, for every \(w\in\mathcal X_W\), summing positive full-data cells with substantive coordinate \(W=w\) yields \(P_{\mathcal M}(W=w)>0\) when \(W\) is always observed.  If \(W\) is partially observed, summing positive full-data cells with \(W=w\) and \(R_W=1\) gives
\[
 P_{\mathcal M}(W=w,R_W=1)>0.
\]
By ass:proxy-consistency this is
\[
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}(W^{\dagger}=w,R_W=1)>0,
\]
so every declared substantive value occurs in the conditional proxy support.  Conversely, proxy consistency permits no value outside \(\mathcal X_W\) on \(R_W=1\).  Thus
\[
 |S_W|=|\mathcal X_W|
 \quad\text{for always-observed }W,
 \qquad
 |S_W^{\dagger}|=|\mathcal X_W|
 \quad\text{for partially observed }W.
\]

In the constructed common law, \(S_Z=\{0,1,2\}\), so any substantive alphabet realizing that observed coordinate has at least three elements.  In particular, no model matching \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) can make every substantive variable binary.  Finally, replace the isolated alphabet \(\mathcal X_Z\) by \(\{0,\ldots,m-1\}\) and take \(E_Z\) uniform on it, for any integer \(m\geq2\).  The same two response models on \((A,Y)\) still have identical observed laws and the same distinct query values.  The forests \(\mathcal F'\subseteq\mathcal F\), their districts, roots, colors, and trace family are unchanged, because \(Z\) is isolated and does not belong to either forest, whereas the attained support lower bound for \(Z\) is \(m\).  Since \(m\) is arbitrary, the smallest required substantive alphabet vector cannot be determined from the color and district structure of the colored hedge alone.  This completes every assertion of the theorem.

statements.statement:
Let \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{lm}}(\mathcal G)\) have finite endogenous alphabets and the mutually independent individual-edge and private factors indexed by \(\mathcal J=\mathcal E^{\leftrightarrow}(\mathcal G)\sqcup\mathcal V\sqcup\mathcal R\). There is a label-compatible deterministic response representation in which every factor has support at most \(K_{\mathcal G}\), the factors remain mutually independent, and, simultaneously for all full cells and all \((a,y)\),
\[
P(V=v,R=r)=P_{\mathcal M}(v,r),
\qquad
P(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a))=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y).
\]
statements.proof_tex:
Put
\[
d=\left|\mathcal X_{\mathcal V}\times\mathcal X_{\mathcal R}\right|+
|\mathcal X_A||\mathcal X_Y|.
\]
We first prove the finite-dimensional support fact needed below. Let \(z:\Omega\to[0,1]^d\) be measurable on a probability space and let \(m=\int z\,d\mu\). If \(S=z(\Omega)\), then \(m\in\operatorname{conv}(S)\). Indeed, let \(K=\overline{\operatorname{conv}(S)}\). If \(m\) is in the relative interior of \(K\), then \(m\in\operatorname{ri}(K)=\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{conv}(S))\subseteq\operatorname{conv}(S)\). If \(m\) is on the relative boundary, a supporting affine functional \(L\) satisfies \(L(x)\geq L(m)\) for \(x\in K\). Since
\[
0=L(m)-L(m)=\int\{L(z(\omega))-L(m)\}\,d\mu(\omega)
\]
and the integrand is nonnegative, \(L(z)=L(m)\) almost surely. Restricting to this proper affine face lowers the affine dimension. Induction on that dimension proves \(m\in\operatorname{conv}(S)\). Finally, if a representation of \(m\) uses more than \(d+1\) points of \(S\), their augmented vectors \((1,z_i)\in\mathbb R^{d+1}\) are linearly dependent. Moving the weights along a nonzero dependence until one weight becomes zero preserves both their sum and their barycenter. Repetition leaves at most \(d+1\) points. Thus there are \(u_1,\ldots,u_k\in\Omega\) and \(\alpha_i\geq0\), with \(k\leq d+1\), \(\sum_i\alpha_i=1\), and
\[
\int z\,d\mu=\sum_{i=1}^k\alpha_i z(u_i).
\]

Now enumerate the finite factor index set \(\mathcal J\). For a current factor \(U_h\), hold its value equal to \(u\), integrate the deterministic acyclic structural evaluation over all other independent factors, and form the vector
\[
z_h(u)=\left(
P(V=v,R=r\mid U_h=u)_{v,r},
P(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a),U_h=u)_{a,y}
\right)\in[0,1]^d.
\]
Independence of the factors gives the current full-cell and intervention vector as \(\int z_h,dP_{U_h}\). The support fact replaces \(P_{U_h}\) by a distribution on at most \(d+1\) actual values of \(U_h\) without changing any coordinate of this vector. This replacement preserves independence because only one marginal factor law is changed. Repeating over the finite set \(\mathcal J\) therefore preserves, at every step, all full-cell probabilities and every queried interventional probability.

It remains to check the declared support budget. Let
\[
S_0=\sum_{Z\in\mathcal V\cup\mathcal R}|\mathcal X_Z|,
\qquad
L_0=\prod_{Z\in\mathcal V\cup\mathcal R}|\mathcal X_Z|.
\]
Every multiplier in the definition of \(N_{\mathcal G}\) is at least one, so \(N_{\mathcal G}\geq S_0\). Also \(L_0\leq2^{S_0}\), and \(|\mathcal X_A||\mathcal X_Y|\leq L_0\). The distinct values \(a_0,a_1\) imply \(N_{\mathcal G}\geq2\). Hence
\[
d+1\leq2L_0+1\leq2^{S_0+2}
\leq2^{N_{\mathcal G}+2}
\leq2^{2^{N_{\mathcal G}}}=K_{\mathcal G}.
\]
Pad each reduced factor with zero-probability states up to \(K_{\mathcal G}\). Restrict the original structural equations to the selected factor values and extend them arbitrarily on padded states. Because the original equations obey every label deletion, the restricted and extended tables can be chosen in \(\mathcal T_{\mathcal G}\). Acyclic deterministic evaluation is unchanged on all positive-probability factor states, which proves the two displayed equalities and the lemma.

statements.statement:
For every \(\mathcal G(H,m)\in\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{EIPFD}}\), every \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G(H,m))\), every \(a\in\mathcal X_A\), and every \(y\in\mathcal X_Y\), writing \(h\) for a joint value of the always-observed logistics block \(H\),
\[
Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)=
\sum_hP_{\mathcal M}(h)
\sum_{b\in\mathcal X_{B_1}}P_{\mathcal M}(b\mid a,h,R_W=0)
\sum_{a'\in\mathcal X_A}P_{\mathcal M}(y\mid b,a',h,R_W=0)
P_{\mathcal M}(a'\mid h,R_W=0).
\]
Every probability on the right is an observed-law probability.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\mathcal G(H,m)\), \(\mathcal M\), \(a\), and \(y\). Strict positivity makes every conditional probability below well defined. The only arrows leaving \(H\) enter \(R_W\), and after intervention on \(A\) every directed path from \(H\) or \(R_W\) to \(Y\) through the treatment equation is cut. The individual-edge factorization supplies no unshown common factor between \(H\cup\{R_W\}\) and the outcome-side variables. Consequently the structural equations give
\[
Y(a)\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}R_W\mid H,
\qquad
P_{\mathcal M}(H=h\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a))=P_{\mathcal M}(h).
\]
By total probability and the first independence,
\[
Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)
=\sum_hP_{\mathcal M}(h)
P_{\mathcal M}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a),h,R_W=0).
\tag{1}
\]

In the selected graph \(R_W=0\), the label semantics deletes \(W\to A\). The vertex \(B_1\) intercepts every directed path from \(A\) to \(Y\); there is no open back-door path from \(A\) to \(B_1\); and conditioning on \(A,H,R_W\) blocks every back-door path from \(B_1\) to \(Y\). In particular, the path through \(A\leftrightarrow Y\) is blocked at \(A\) in the last check, while paths reaching \(Y\) through \(B_m\to Y\) make \(Y\) a collider when paired with \(A\leftrightarrow Y\). Running the ordinary identification steps certified by \(\text{lem:ordinary-id-soundness}\) in this selected graph gives, equation by equation,
\[
P(b\mid\operatorname{do}(a),h,R_W=0)=P(b\mid a,h,R_W=0),
\tag{2}
\]
\[
P(y\mid\operatorname{do}(b),h,R_W=0)
=\sum_{a'}P(y\mid b,a',h,R_W=0)P(a'\mid h,R_W=0),
\tag{3}
\]
and, because \(B_1\) intercepts all directed \(A\)-to-\(Y\) paths,
\[
P(y\mid\operatorname{do}(a),h,R_W=0)
=\sum_bP(b\mid a,h,R_W=0)P(y\mid\operatorname{do}(b),h,R_W=0).
\tag{4}
\]
Substitution of (3) into (4), followed by substitution into (1), is exactly the displayed formula. The variables \(H,A,B_1,Y,R_W\) are always observed except that \(R_W\) is itself an observed indicator, so proxy consistency shows that every factor on the right is a functional of \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\).

statements.statement:
Let an exact specialization on a negative partition cell yield \(\omega=(a,y,\theta^0,\theta^1)\) satisfying \(\mathsf W_j\). Decoding the two response vectors gives \(\mathcal M_0,\mathcal M_1\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) such that
\[
P_{\mathcal M_0}(\mathcal O)=P_{\mathcal M_1}(\mathcal O)=P_{\mathrm{obs}},
\qquad
Q_a^{\mathcal M_0}(y)\neq Q_a^{\mathcal M_1}(y).
\]
The factors in both decoded models retain the individual-edge product structure and every full-data cell is strictly positive.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(K\) be the ordered subfield of \(\mathbb R\) generated by the specialized observed coordinates \(\mathbf p=(P_{\mathrm{obs}}(o))_o\), and let \(K^{\mathrm{rc}}\) be its real closure. By \(\text{def:exact-observed-specialization}\), the exact negative-cell sample consists of Thom-encoded vectors \(\theta^0,\theta^1\) over \(K^{\mathrm{rc}}\). The statement that \(\omega\) satisfies \(\mathsf W_j\) means, by \(\text{def:terminal-qe-test}\) and \(\text{def:symbolic-observed-partition}\), that
\[
\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta^i;\mathbf p)\quad(i=0,1),
\qquad
q_{a,y}(\theta^0)\neq q_{a,y}(\theta^1).
\tag{1}
\]
This use of Thom encodings does not assert that the coordinates are algebraic over \(\mathbb Q\): they are algebraic over \(K\), as required by the corrected specialization definition.

Apply the converse direction of \(\text{thm:response-fiber-equivalence}\) separately to the two compatibility assertions in (1). It gives decoded models \(\mathcal M_i\) such that
\[
\mathcal M_i\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}}),
\qquad
p_{v,r}(\theta^i)=P_{\mathcal M_i}(v,r),
\qquad
q_{a',y'}(\theta^i)=Q_{a'}^{\mathcal M_i}(y')
\tag{2}
\]
for \(i\in\{0,1\}\) and every \((v,r,a',y')\). The equality constraints in \(\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}\) further give
\[
P_{\mathcal M_i}(\mathcal O=o)=p_o(\theta^i)=P_{\mathrm{obs}}(o)
\quad\text{for every }o\in\mathcal X_{\mathcal O}.
\tag{3}
\]
The strict inequalities in the same formula give
\[
P_{\mathcal M_i}(v,r)=p_{v,r}(\theta^i)>0
\quad\text{for every }(v,r),
\tag{4}
\]
so both decoded full-data laws satisfy the required support condition. Finally, the one-hot equations select one label-compatible response-table tuple, while the latent mass of a joint state is \(\prod_h\rho^i_{h,u_h}\). Thus the decoding in (2) retains one mutually independent factor for every individual bidirected edge and every private factor; it does not introduce a district-wide mixture.

Taking \((a',y')=(a,y)\) in (2) and substituting into the inequality in (1) yields
\[
Q_a^{\mathcal M_0}(y)=q_{a,y}(\theta^0)\neq q_{a,y}(\theta^1)=Q_a^{\mathcal M_1}(y).
\tag{5}
\]
Equations (2)--(5) prove all claims.

statements.statement: The formulas \(\mathscr P_{\mathcal G,A,Y}\) form a finite semialgebraic partition of the feasible projection \(\{\mathbf p:\exists\theta\,\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p)\}\). For every compatible \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), every \(a\), and every \(y\), the unique cell containing \((P_{\mathrm{obs}}(o))_o\) carries a unique value for \(q_{a,y}\) if and only if \(\mathcal M\mapsto Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)\) is constant on \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\). Otherwise it carries \(\mathsf W_j\); under \(\operatorname{Exact}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), a sample from \(\mathsf W_j\) decodes to the positive same-observed, different-query pair of \(\text{lem:negative-cell-model-pair}\).
statements.proof_tex:
For each \((a,y)\), \(\mathsf I_{a,y}(\mathcal G;\mathbf p)\) is a first-order formula over a real closed field whose atomic formulas are polynomial sign conditions. By \(\text{lem:real-closed-field-quantifier-elimination}\), eliminating \(\theta^0,\theta^1\) produces a quantifier-free formula in \(\mathbf p\) with the same truth value. Apply the same result to the feasible-projection formula \(\exists\theta\,\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p)\). Only finitely many polynomials occur because the graph, response-table set, latent alphabets, treatment alphabet, and outcome alphabet are finite.

By \(\text{lem:finite-sign-invariant-cad}\), those finitely many polynomials admit one finite sign-invariant cylindrical algebraic decomposition. On each cell every atomic sign and hence every Boolean combination above has a constant truth value. Intersecting with the feasible projection and discarding empty cells therefore yields finitely many pairwise-disjoint semialgebraic cells whose union is exactly
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathrm{feas}}
=\{\mathbf p:\exists\theta\,\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p)\}.
\tag{1}
\]
This is precisely the common-CAD construction in \(\text{def:symbolic-observed-partition}\), so its cell formulas are \(\psi_1,\ldots,\psi_J\). In particular, every compatible observed-law vector in (1) belongs to exactly one such cell; the common construction does not identify states merely because their shortened graphical keys agree.

Fix a compatible \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), its unique cell, and \((a,y)\). Expanding \(\text{def:terminal-qe-test}\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf I_{a,y}(\mathcal G;\mathbf p)
&\Longleftrightarrow
\neg\exists\theta^0,\theta^1\bigl[
\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta^0;\mathbf p)
\wedge\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta^1;\mathbf p)
\wedge q_{a,y}(\theta^0)\neq q_{a,y}(\theta^1)
\bigr]\\
&\Longleftrightarrow
q_{a,y}\text{ is constant on }
\Theta(\mathbf p),
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
where \(\Theta(\mathbf p)=\{\theta:\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p)\}\). The forward direction of \(\text{thm:response-fiber-equivalence}\) sends every \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) to an element \(\theta_{\mathcal M}\in\Theta(\mathbf p)\) and preserves
\[
q_{a,y}(\theta_{\mathcal M})=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y).
\tag{3}
\]
Its converse sends every \(\theta\in\Theta(\mathbf p)\) to a model \(\mathcal M_\theta\) in that fiber and preserves the same equality. Consequently,
\[
q_{a,y}\text{ is constant on }\Theta(\mathbf p)
\Longleftrightarrow
\mathcal M\longmapsto Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)
\text{ is constant on }\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}}).
\tag{4}
\]

On the true side of (2), compatibility makes \(\Theta(\mathbf p)\) nonempty, and
\[
\mathsf V_{a,y}(\mathbf p,z)
\Longleftrightarrow
\exists\theta\in\Theta(\mathbf p)\,[z=q_{a,y}(\theta)]
\tag{5}
\]
therefore holds for exactly one \(z\). On the false side of (2), negating the universal equality yields two compatible response vectors with unequal query values; the unnegated conjunction is exactly the stored relation \(\mathsf W_j\).

Under \(\operatorname{Exact}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), \(\text{def:exact-observed-specialization}\) decides the finitely many cell signs and, on a negative cell, represents a satisfying pair by Thom encodings over the real closure of the ordered field generated by \(\mathbf p\). Applying \(\text{lem:negative-cell-model-pair}\) to that pair gives the strictly positive, individual-edge-factorized models with equal observed law and unequal causal coordinate asserted in the final sentence. Equations (1)--(5) prove the dichotomy.

statements.statement: Let \(\Phi(Y)\) be a first-order formula over a real closed field whose atoms are polynomial sign conditions, with \(Y\) the free-variable block. There exists a quantifier-free polynomial-sign formula \(\Psi(Y)\) such that \(\Phi(y)\) and \(\Psi(y)\) have the same truth value for every \(y\).

source.verbatim_statement: There exists a quantifier-free formula, \(\Psi(Y)\), such that for any \(y\in R^\ell\), \(\Phi(y)\) is true if and only if \(\Psi(y)\) is true.

statements.statement:
Fix a compatible observed law \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) and a coordinate \((a,y)\). If the TCF cell containing \((P_{\mathrm{obs}}(o))_o\) is negative for that coordinate, then there exist \(\mathcal M_0,\mathcal M_1\in\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G)\) such that
\[
P_{\mathcal M_0}(\mathcal O)=P_{\mathcal M_1}(\mathcal O)=P_{\mathrm{obs}},
\qquad
Q_a^{\mathcal M_0}(y)\neq Q_a^{\mathcal M_1}(y).
\]
Consequently \(Q_a(y)\) is not identified over the larger published ambient set \(\{\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{lm}}(\mathcal G):P_{\mathcal M}(\mathcal O)=P_{\mathrm{obs}}\}\). This existential conclusion does not require \(\operatorname{Exact}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\); exactness is required only to algorithmically extract a represented witness pair.
statements.justification: A finite-subclass witness is already an ambient-class witness, so negative TCF cells have a direct published-model interpretation.
statements.gap: The constructive exact-specialization interface is stronger than is logically needed for nonidentification; existential nonconstancy transfers without an exact representation.
statements.consumer: A negative ADHD medication or test-achievement coordinate certifies failure of ambient lm-SCM identification even when no numerical witness extraction oracle is supplied.

sampling_model.design: Population exact recovery from a known finite regular-maximal labeled-missingness graph, expressed as a symbolic semialgebraic partition of feasible observed-cell coordinates; graph discovery and finite-sample inference are outside the core.
sampling_model.units: Independent draws of the observed record \(\mathcal O\) are the eventual statistical input, while the identification theorems treat the observed cells as formal population parameters.
sampling_model.treatment: A supplied intervention value \(a\in\mathcal X_A\) for the substantive treatment \(A\).
sampling_model.overlap: Strict positivity of the finite full-data law ensures that every selected trace denominator used by the calculus is nonzero.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Not part of this exact-identification core; exact point specialization requires rational or algebraic cells with isolating data, or an exact-real sign oracle, and arbitrary population reals are not claimed to be computational inputs.

estimand_functional: On a partition cell identifying every outcome coordinate at \(a_0\) and \(a_1\), \(\tau_{s_Y}=\sum_{y\in\mathcal X_Y}s_Y(y)\{f_{a_1,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)-f_{a_0,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\}\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 4 states that if \(K,H,\{L_r\}_r\) satisfy conditions \(\mathrm{(i)}\)--\(\mathrm{(v)}\), then equations \(\mathrm{(5)}\)--\(\mathrm{(7)}\) recover \(P(Y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a))\) and the NATE as weighted context functionals.
Its algorithm is sound and complete when the context variables are observed causal roots.
Its search always terminates and any returned expression is correct, without a general completeness result.
Its partial-order recursion handles missing-data subproblems but leaves completeness for general DAG models open.
Any two valid fixing sequences for the same set yield the same reachable graph and kernel.
Definition 6 defines a hedge and Theorem 4 makes it a nonidentifiability witness; Theorem 6 and Corollary 2 connect recursive ID failure to that obstruction and establish completeness.
Finite discrete causal queries and evidence can be encoded as polynomial optimization problems over response functions.

tldr: Finite labeled-missingness graphs encode mechanism shifts caused by missing inputs, but existing NATE procedures can discard identifying information by restricting to a context before deriving an available kernel. The observed-law-indexed procedure \(\operatorname{TCF}(\mathcal G,A,Y,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) works symbolically in the observed-cell coordinates and constructs a finite semialgebraic partition whose cells carry either a unique query functional or a non-singleton-fiber certificate formula. Its response-function variables preserve every individual bidirected-edge factor of the published semi-Markovian graph. An exact-law specialization may extract an algebraic pair, which an independent first-divergence theorem compiles into a colored hedge and two strictly positive same-observed, different-query lm-SCMs. TCF preserves the exact functionals of de Aguas et al. Proposition 4 and the Mokhtarian et al. root-control procedure and strictly contains both on the parameterized endogenous-indicator proxy front-door class, with \(\mathcal G_\star\) providing a fully worked delayed-selection member.

project_justification.gap: De Aguas et al. give a sufficient weighted-adjustment criterion and the Figure 3(b) fix-before-select recovery; Mokhtarian et al. give completeness only for observed root controls. CSI search, missing-data recursion, and ordinary hedges do not jointly preserve label licenses, proxy traces, strict positivity, and the individual-edge semi-Markovian factorization.
project_justification.niche: Finite positive regular-maximal lm-graphs admit exact observed-cell algebra, provided the response-function variables respect each bidirected edge rather than replacing an entire district by one unrestricted latent table. The missing graphical object is a reachable kernel carrying both its context license and its derivation trace.
project_justification.fill: The proposal supplies that colored kernel, a two-way edge-factorized response-function equivalence, a symbolic semialgebraic partition theorem with an exact-input specialization contract, a concrete finite CAD bound, soundness, and an independent first-divergence compiler establishing colored-hedge completeness. It preserves both published comparator functionals and proves strict containment through the explicit delayed-selection functional on \(\mathcal G_\star\) and its parameterized EIPFD family.

technical_internal_limitation: The two high-risk steps are finite edgewise support reduction and the graphical converse. The compiler theorem must prove that every nonconstant fiber produces the stated first-divergent district invariant; only then does the Shpitser--Pearl forest argument extend to label licenses, recorded proxy histories, nonzero full-data cells, and individual-edge latent factorization. The symbolic CAD wrapper merely partitions the observed-cell parameter space and cannot substitute for that graphical proof. A shared district mixture is unavailable because it would violate the advertised semi-Markovian graph. The adjacent-swap lemma is local and does not claim that context restriction commutes with fixing; Figure 3(b) rules out that stronger statement.
honest_scope: The graph, labels, finite alphabets, outcome score map \(s_Y\), treatment, and outcome are supplied. Identification is stated symbolically over the feasible observed-cell coordinates and mathematically specialized to every nonempty finite-state, semi-Markovian, strictly positive, regular-maximal observational fiber. Numerical cell selection is defined only for rational or real-algebraic observed laws with isolating data, or through an exact-real polynomial-sign oracle; no ordinary computation on arbitrary population reals is claimed. TCF outputs a partition with value or witness formulas, while colored hedges and paired models are conclusions of the independent first-divergence compiler theorem. The explicit bound proves finite termination and makes no polynomial-time claim. Estimation, graph learning, continuous variables, nonpositive support, and finite-sample inference are outside the core. Ordinary ID, the Mokhtarian root-control functional, and de Aguas Proposition 4 are exact reductions. Finite edgewise support reduction, general colored-hedge realization, and binary-alphabet sufficiency are the principal proof obligations.
